def: A reader of the record of what an agent did, which rates how suspicious each part looks and sends the worst to a person.
Monitoring that runs after the fact on a stored log, not in the path of each action.
The fraction of items a person has time to read, which fixes the monitor's threshold.
A careful review, by a trusted person or model, of an item the monitor flagged.
A control protocol in which a weaker model that is trusted rates how suspicious the untrusted model's output looks.
A control protocol in which a second copy of the untrusted model rates the output, with steps to prevent collusion.
A control protocol in which a trusted model edits suspicious output to remove anything that looks like a backdoor.
A control rule that replaces suspicious output with the trusted model's own answer when it is not suspicious enough to audit.
The probability that no attack succeeds over a whole run when the untrusted model plays the red team's best attack.
How much correct work a protocol gets when the untrusted model is honest, scaled so the trusted model alone scores 0 and the untrusted model alone scores 1.
Two copies of an untrusted model coordinating so that one hides the other's attack, which redaction aims to prevent.
Removing information that could carry a collusion signal from what the monitor sees.
